refs.title: Athenaeum of Philadelphia - Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia
refs.note: States: 'Architect John Notman developed a three-story brownstone Italianate Renaissance Revival building designed to hold the Athenaeum's collections on the second floor.' Note the compound label -- the piano nobile is stated, which is the one fact the renaissance-revival-american kit's own `piano_nobile_min_ratio` depends on.

refs.title: Visit - The Athenaeum of Philadelphia
refs.note: Owner. Gives the address as 219 S. 6th Street, 'East side of Washington Square below Walnut St.'

refs.title: The Athenaeum of Philadelphia Refreshed With Facade Renovation - Hidden City Philadelphia
refs.note: Records that the National Register listed the Athenaeum in 1972 and that it was designated a National Historic Landmark four years later, and that it is a contributing structure in the Society Hill Historic District. No reference number is given there, so none is recorded.

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026, WP-11.3 Tranche 2, the mid-nineteenth-century city house cluster. A HABS survey EXISTS for this building and has no words in it: PA-1389 is photographs and reduced copies of measured drawings, and its data file is one cover sheet. That is a different gap from 'no survey', and the distinction matters to anyone costing this work -- the figures the corpus wants are drawn, digitised, and unreadable from this container. The Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia supplies the one thing the kit needs in words: three storeys with the collections, and therefore the tall room, on the SECOND floor.
